plate_findings.evidence: Caption and in-text description identify sheets of foamy macrophages/histiocytes separating bony trabeculae.
Caption explicitly states that bony trabeculae are separated by fibrosis; H&E shows prominent fibrotic tissue.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Tibial H&E biopsy from a patient with Erdheim-Chester disease showing fibrosis and xanthomatous foamy histiocytic infiltration. B: CD68 immunohistochemistry demonstrates the dense histiocytic infiltrate characteristic of the Erdheim-Chester tibial biopsy. C: Factor XIIIa immunohistochemistry highlights histiocytes in the Erdheim-Chester tibial lesion. D: S-100 staining is largely negative in the Erdheim-Chester histiocytic infiltrate, with only a focal S-100-positive area described in the text.

panels.figure_caption: Histological sample from the tibia of patient #1. (A) H&E. Bony trabeculae separated by fibrosis and sheets of foamy macrophages. (B) Histiocytes demonstrating intense granular staining for CD68. (C) Histiocytes demonstrating patchy staining for factor XIIIa. (D) S-100 protein staining of the biopsy specimen.

A microscopic examination of the tibial biopsy revealed bony trabeculae separated by a xanthomatous, diffuse spindle cell macrophage population with few interspersed giant cells (Figure 4A). The spindle cells stained relatively uniformly for the presence of CD163, and in a more patchy fashion but quite strongly for factor XIIIa (Figure 4C), surface staining for CD14 and granular intense staining for CD68 (Figure 4B). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of yellowish periorbital xanthelasma-like lesions in a patient described in the Erdheim-Chester disease case series; the appearance is a recognized cutaneous manifestation. [raw subtype: cutaneous] B: Clinical photograph of a discrete red-yellow papule on the right flank in a patient with Erdheim-Chester disease; it is consistent with the cutaneous xanthomatous lesions described in the article. Upon an elaborated history, the patient disclosed suffering from mild lower limb pain, loss of libido and increased thirst and urination for the past seven years, as well. 12 years prior to her current presentation and also suffered from recurrent urinary tract infections. Her physical examination was unremarkable aside from periorbital xanthelasma-like lesions (Figure 8A). Abnormal laboratory findings included a microcytic iron deficiency anemia (hemoglobin: 11 g/dL, MCV: 77.5 fL, iron: 19 μg/dL) and an elevated ESR (98 mm/hr). Both protein electrophoresis and tumor markers were without pathological findings.
